frontmatter.title: Online Business Asset Purchase Reviewer Checklist
frontmatter.description: Reviewer checks for the asset sale, its optional terms and the conditions that make each safeguard relevant.
frontmatter.coverage: General core plus optional internet-business operating profile

requirements.requirementGuidance: Match every payment, conveyance and signature obligation to a named party. The agreement SHOULD identify each purchaser and seller by legal name and signing capacity. Entity/individual capacity and additional asset owners remain fact-dependent. Drafting context.

sources.title: Greenfield Online–Dohring asset purchase agreement (2004), parties
sources.proposition: The Greenfield Online agreement made the selling company's shareholder a party solely for purposes of Section 9.7.
sources.verbatimQuote: This ASSET PURCHASE AGREEMENT (this “Agreement”), dated as of August 18th, 2004, is by and among GREENFIELD ONLINE, INC., a Delaware corporation having its principal offices located at 21 River Road, Wilton, Connecticut 06897 (“Buyer”) and THE DOHRING COMPANY, a California corporation, having its principal offices located at 412 West Broadway, Third Floor, Glendale, CA 91204 (“Seller”) and, solely for purposes of Section 9.7 hereof, DOUG C. DOHRING (“Shareholder”).

sources.title: Meta Financial–Fort Knox asset purchase agreement (2015), individual joinder
sources.proposition: The Meta Financial agreement bound an individual as a shareholder solely for purposes of three listed sections.
sources.verbatimQuote: Lodge agrees that solely for purposes of Section 10.1(b), Section 10.3 and Section 10.6, he shall be included in the definition of “Shareholder” and shall be bound by the obligations of a Shareholder as set forth therein.

requirements.requirementGuidance: Trace the operative grant to assets; flag stock, membership interests or alternative transaction branches. The agreement SHOULD identify the transaction as a transfer of specified assets rather than a transfer of ownership interests in the seller. Equity or mixed transactions require separately scoped review. Drafting context.

sources.title: Asset purchase vs. stock purchase, owner shares (The Mellor Law Firm)
sources.citation: Mark Mellor, Asset Purchase vs. Stock Purchase: What California Business Buyers Need to Know, The Mellor Law Firm, APLC (May 14, 2026).
sources.proposition: The Mellor Law Firm explains that in a stock purchase the buyer buys the owner's shares in the corporation or limited liability company.
sources.verbatimQuote: In a stock purchase, you buy the owner’s shares in the corporation or LLC.

sources.title: Grove–VitaMedica asset purchase agreement (2021), acquired assets
sources.proposition: The Grove agreement defined its acquired assets as all of the seller's assets other than the excluded assets.
sources.verbatimQuote: The term "Acquired Assets" means all assets of the Seller, other than the Excluded Assets.

requirements.requirementGuidance: For each asset class, locate the grant and a way to identify its members. The agreement SHOULD identify the purchased assets through a schedule or other objectively ascertainable description. The grant may enumerate assets, convey a bounded business-wide category, or both. Drafting context.

sources.title: Imke Ratschko: The Basics of an Asset Purchase Agreement (Ratschko PLLC)
sources.citation: Imke Ratschko, The Basics of an Asset Purchase Agreement, Ratschko PLLC (July 25, 2022; updated July 28, 2022).
sources.proposition: Imke Ratschko supports clearly describing which assets are included and which are excluded.
sources.verbatimQuote: So I recommend that the description makes it very clear which assets are included, and which are excluded.

sources.title: Grove–VitaMedica asset purchase agreement (2021), acquired-assets schedule
sources.proposition: The Grove agreement's acquired assets include those listed on Schedule 2.1(a).
sources.verbatimQuote: The Acquired Assets include, without limitation, those set forth on Schedule 2.1(a) hereto.

requirements.requirementGuidance: Trace every exclusion against the grant; an express none election is assessable. The agreement SHOULD identify assets retained by the seller and resolve conflicts with the purchased-asset description. Cash, receivables, names and shared tools are choices, not automatic exclusions. Drafting context.

sources.title: Imke Ratschko: The Basics of an Asset Purchase Agreement (Ratschko PLLC)
sources.citation: Imke Ratschko, The Basics of an Asset Purchase Agreement, Ratschko PLLC (July 25, 2022; updated July 28, 2022).
sources.proposition: Imke Ratschko supports clearly describing which assets are included and which are excluded.
sources.verbatimQuote: So I recommend that the description makes it very clear which assets are included, and which are excluded.

sources.title: Grove–VitaMedica asset purchase agreement (2021), excluded assets
sources.proposition: The Grove agreement excluded the assets listed on its Schedule 2.1(b) and stated that the excluded assets include the seller's cash.
sources.verbatimQuote: Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, the Acquired Assets shall not include the assets, properties and rights of Seller set forth on Schedule 2.1(b) hereto (collectively, the “Excluded Assets”). The term Excluded Assets includes without limitation cash of Seller.

requirements.requirementGuidance: Match each assumed category to an obligation, period and responsible party. The agreement SHOULD identify the obligations the purchaser expressly assumes. Categories are limited or broadened deliberately; third-party exposure requires separate review. An asset-sale structure does not by itself rule out successor liability, a theory that has expanded over time. Drafting context.

sources.title: Samuel D. Hodson: Successor Liability Risks in Asset Purchase Agreements (Taft)
sources.citation: Samuel D. Hodson, Successor Liability Risks in Asset Purchase Agreements, Taft Law Bulletins (June 26, 2020).
sources.proposition: Samuel D. Hodson supports that an APA assigns responsibility between the parties for the seller’s obligations.
sources.verbatimQuote: The asset purchase agreement assigns responsibility between the parties for the seller’s obligations.

sources.title: Grove–VitaMedica asset purchase agreement (2021), assumed liabilities
sources.proposition: The Grove agreement limited its assumed liabilities to the seller liabilities listed on Schedule 2.2(a).
sources.verbatimQuote: “Assumed Liabilities” means only those Liabilities of Seller set forth on Schedule 2.2(a), which includes a list of the assumed accounts payable of Seller.

sources.title: Successor liability in the purchase of a business, part 1 (Kahn, Dees, Donovan & Kahn), exceptions
sources.citation: Jeffrey K. Helfrich, Successor Liability in the Purchase of a Business: Express or Implied Assumption of Obligations (Part 1 of 8), Kahn, Dees, Donovan & Kahn, LLP (May 5, 2015).
sources.proposition: Kahn, Dees, Donovan & Kahn explains that the traditional rule protects an asset buyer from the seller's debts but that, in some cases, an asset purchaser may be held liable for certain liabilities of the seller.
sources.verbatimQuote: The law in most jurisdictions has traditionally held that when one company sells all of its assets to another, the buyer does not become liable for the debts and liabilities of the selling company. This is still true to a large extent, and we frequently recommend structuring a transaction as an asset purchase in order to protect the buyer from the liabilities of the business being acquired. However, over the past several years, the theory of successor liability has evolved and expanded as a result of a series of clashes between the policy in favor of allowing a company to sell its assets in an unrestricted manner, balanced against other policies, such as providing a source of relief for injured parties or other claimants. As a result, in some cases, a purchaser of assets may be held liable for certain liabilities of the seller.

requirements.requirementGuidance: Read the retained-liability rule together with every assumption and exception. The agreement SHOULD allocate liabilities not expressly assumed to the seller as between the parties. This criterion evaluates the allocation between the contracting parties; third-party exposure requires separate review. A seller's creditors are not parties to the agreement and are not bound by it; a bankruptcy-court or other judicial sale may be an exception. Drafting context.

sources.title: Samuel D. Hodson: Successor Liability Risks in Asset Purchase Agreements (Taft)
sources.citation: Samuel D. Hodson, Successor Liability Risks in Asset Purchase Agreements, Taft Law Bulletins (June 26, 2020).
sources.proposition: Samuel D. Hodson supports that an APA assigns responsibility between the parties for the seller’s obligations.
sources.verbatimQuote: The asset purchase agreement assigns responsibility between the parties for the seller’s obligations.

sources.title: Grove–VitaMedica asset purchase agreement (2021), retained liabilities
sources.proposition: The Grove agreement left every seller liability other than the assumed liabilities with the seller, whenever it arose and whether or not it was disclosed.
sources.verbatimQuote: With the sole exception of the Assumed Liabilities, the Seller shall retain, and the Buyer shall not be obligated to pay, perform or otherwise discharge, any other Liabilities of Seller, whether arising prior to, on or after the Closing Date, whether or not related to the Business and whether or not disclosed to the Buyer (“Retained Liabilities”).

sources.title: Samuel D. Hodson: creditors are not bound by the asset purchase agreement (Taft)
sources.citation: Samuel D. Hodson, Successor Liability Risks in Asset Purchase Agreements, Taft Law Bulletins (June 26, 2020).
sources.proposition: Samuel D. Hodson states that a seller’s creditors are not parties to, or bound by, the asset purchase agreement, noting that bankruptcy-court-ordered and other judicial sales may be an exception.
sources.verbatimQuote: A seller’s creditors are not parties to the asset purchase agreement and are not bound by it. (Sales governed by bankruptcy court orders pursuant to 11 U.S.C. 363 and other judicial sales may be an exception to this rule.)

requirements.requirementGuidance: Locate date, time and treatment of transactions spanning the cutoff. The agreement SHOULD state the effective cutoff for allocating business receipts, expenses and performance between the parties. Closing time and economic effective time may differ if expressly reconciled. Drafting context.

sources.title: Salem Web Network–Gloo asset purchase agreement (2023), accounts receivable cutoff
sources.proposition: The Salem agreement left the seller owning receivables for goods sold and services rendered before closing and required each party to turn over to the other payments it received that belonged to the other.
sources.verbatimQuote: Buyer acknowledges that Seller is retaining ownership of all accounts receivable of the Business for goods sold and services rendered by Seller prior to the Closing Date and that such accounts receivable are Excluded Assets (the “Seller Accounts Receivable”). From and after the Closing Date, Seller shall be permitted to contact account debtors with respect to any of the Seller Accounts Receivable for purposes of collection thereof and to instruct account debtors to remit payments for the Seller Accounts Receivable directly to Seller. Buyer shall promptly remit, turnover and endorse to Seller any payments representing Seller Accounts Receivable received by Buyer after the Closing Date. From and after the Closing Seller shall promptly remit, turnover and endorse to Buyer any payments representing accounts receivable arising from the sale of goods or services by the Business after the Closing Date.

sources.title: OW Holdings–Sitestar asset purchase agreement (2007), prorations
sources.proposition: The Sitestar agreement prorated taxes, utilities, rents and similar charges benefiting both parties at closing, based on the actual number of days of pre-closing and post-closing use.
sources.verbatimQuote: Any real estate, personal property, and other taxes, utilities, rents, charges, license charges and other assessments that inure to the benefit of both Seller and Buyer, if any, shall be prorated at the Closing between Seller and Buyer based on the actual number of days applicable to pre-Closing and post-Closing use.

requirements.requirementGuidance: Only if intellectual property is included, review the following safeguard. Otherwise mark it not applicable. Trace material IP to creation or acquisition records and identify missing assignments. The agreement SHOULD require disclosure of the basis on which the seller owns the intellectual property being transferred. Qualifiers and remediation for missing records remain negotiable. Drafting context.

sources.title: Luna–Micron asset purchase agreement (2018), IP ownership
sources.proposition: The Luna agreement represented that the seller was the sole and exclusive legal and beneficial owner of its IP registrations and IP assets, free and clear of encumbrances, without representing their enforceability.
sources.verbatimQuote: Seller is the sole and exclusive legal and beneficial owner of all right, title, and interest in and to the Intellectual Property Registrations and Intellectual Property Assets, free and clear of Encumbrances (it being understood and acknowledged that the foregoing representation and warranty does not constitute a representation and warranty of enforceability of any such Intellectual Property Registrations and Intellectual Property Assets).

sources.title: Salem asset purchase agreement (2023), owned and licensed intellectual property
sources.proposition: The Salem seller represented that it solely owned the business intellectual property other than third-party intellectual property licensed to it under contracts listed on Schedule 1.1(c).
sources.verbatimQuote: Except for all rights in Intellectual Property related to the Business that are owned by a third party and licensed to Seller under a Business IP Contract listed as such on Schedule 1.1(c) (“Licensed Business IP”), Seller has sole and exclusive ownership of all right, title, and interest in and to, and has good, valid and marketable title to, all other Business Intellectual Property (“Owned Business IP”), free and clear of any Liens, and has the sole and exclusive right to use and otherwise exploit such Intellectual Property without payment to any third party.

sources.title: Bankrate asset purchase agreement (2016), owned and licensed intellectual property
sources.proposition: The Bankrate seller represented that it exclusively owned the intellectual property used in its business, other than intellectual property licensed to it as identified in Schedule 4.10(d).
sources.verbatimQuote: Seller exclusively owns all right, title and interest in and to all Intellectual Property used in connection with the operation and conduct of its business, free and clear of any Liens (other than Permitted Liens), other than Intellectual Property that is licensed to Seller as identified in Schedule 4.10(d) or Intellectual Property that is licensed to Seller and not required to be identified in Schedule 4.10(d).

requirements.requirementGuidance: Only if intellectual property is included, review the following safeguard. Otherwise mark it not applicable. Locate the conveyance and identify any separate instrument needed to complete it. The agreement SHOULD provide an operative transfer mechanism for the included intellectual property. Instrument form and formalities require asset- and jurisdiction-specific review. Drafting context.

sources.title: Greenfield–Dohring asset purchase agreement (2004), copyright assignment at closing
sources.proposition: The Greenfield agreement’s closing documents included an assignment and bill of sale, an assignment of trademarks, an assignment of copyrights and any other assignments needed to transfer the assets.
sources.verbatimQuote: Such documents shall include, without limitation, an Assignment and Bill of Sale in the form attached hereto as Exhibit 2.5, an Assignment of Trademarks in the form attached hereto as Exhibit 2.5(a), an Assignment of Copyrights in the form attached hereto as Exhibit 2.5(b), and any assignments or other documents necessary to effect such transfer and conveyance of the Transferred Assets.

sources.title: Grove–VitaMedica asset purchase agreement (2021), closing documents
sources.proposition: The Grove agreement required the selling parties to deliver at closing a bill of sale and assignment and separate assignments of patents, trademarks and copyrights.
sources.verbatimQuote: The Selling Parties shall deliver to the Buyer: (i) A Bill of Sale and Assignment in the form of Exhibit E executed by Seller; and (ii) An Assignment of Patents, Assignment of Servicemarks and Trademarks and Assignment of Copyrights in the form of Exhibits F-1, F-2 and F-3 executed by Seller; and (iii) Non-Competition Agreements in the form of Exhibit G (the "Selling Parties’ Non-Competition Agreements") executed by each of the Selling Parties;

requirements.requirementGuidance: Only if third-party dependencies exist, review the following safeguard. Otherwise mark it not applicable. Locate license/provider, covered component and restriction information for each material dependency. The agreement SHOULD identify third-party rights needed to use the transferred business assets. Open-source, commercial, stock-media and hosted-service dependencies merit separate entries. Drafting context.

sources.title: Luna–Micron asset purchase agreement (2018)
sources.proposition: The Luna agreement supports identifying IP agreements by date, title and parties in its disclosure schedule.
sources.verbatimQuote: Schedule 3.25(b) contains a correct, current and complete list of all Intellectual Property Agreements, specifying for each the date, title and parties thereto.

sources.title: Salem asset purchase agreement (2023), owned and licensed intellectual property
sources.proposition: The Salem seller represented that it solely owned the business intellectual property other than third-party intellectual property licensed to it under contracts listed on Schedule 1.1(c).
sources.verbatimQuote: Except for all rights in Intellectual Property related to the Business that are owned by a third party and licensed to Seller under a Business IP Contract listed as such on Schedule 1.1(c) (“Licensed Business IP”), Seller has sole and exclusive ownership of all right, title, and interest in and to, and has good, valid and marketable title to, all other Business Intellectual Property (“Owned Business IP”), free and clear of any Liens, and has the sole and exclusive right to use and otherwise exploit such Intellectual Property without payment to any third party.

sources.title: Bankrate asset purchase agreement (2016), owned and licensed intellectual property
sources.proposition: The Bankrate seller represented that it exclusively owned the intellectual property used in its business, other than intellectual property licensed to it as identified in Schedule 4.10(d).
sources.verbatimQuote: Seller exclusively owns all right, title and interest in and to all Intellectual Property used in connection with the operation and conduct of its business, free and clear of any Liens (other than Permitted Liens), other than Intellectual Property that is licensed to Seller as identified in Schedule 4.10(d) or Intellectual Property that is licensed to Seller and not required to be identified in Schedule 4.10(d).

requirements.requirementGuidance: Only if operation depends on retained intellectual property, review the following safeguard. Otherwise mark it not applicable. Locate permitted use, duration and termination terms for the retained dependency. The agreement SHOULD specify the purchaser's post-closing use rights in retained seller intellectual property needed by the business. License, replacement or elimination of the dependency are alternatives. Drafting context.

sources.title: Salem asset purchase agreement (2023), license to shared code
sources.proposition: The Salem agreement gave the buyer a royalty-free, perpetual, noncancellable worldwide license to use the shared code for the websites and the business.
sources.verbatimQuote: Buyer shall have the royalty-free, perpetual, noncancellable worldwide license to use the Shared Code with respect to the Websites and the Business.

sources.title: ECOtality–Blink Acquisition asset purchase agreement (2013), interim use of retained name and domain
sources.proposition: The ECOtality agreement kept the Ecotality name and domain with the sellers until a later effective transfer date and, until then, let the buyer use the domain without charge by linking to its acquired business.
sources.verbatimQuote: Buyer acknowledges and agrees that the name Ecotality (together with any and all derivatives thereof, websites, domain name, email addresses social media accounts, tradenames, logos and other intellectual property related thereto, the “ Ecotality Name ”) shall remain the property of Sellers until the end of the Bankruptcy Period at which time the transfer of the Ecotality Name to Buyer hereunder shall become effective. Until such time as the transfer of the Ecotality Name becomes effective, Sellers shall permit Buyer and the purchasers of the Minit-Charger and eTec Labs businesses to use, without charge, the Ecotality domain name by permitting such parties to place links to their respective businesses acquired from Sellers on the Ecotality website.
sources.pullQuoteLocator: Buyer acknowledges and agrees that the|Sellers on the Ecotality website.

requirements.requirementGuidance: Only if customer or vendor contracts are involved, review the following safeguard. Otherwise mark it not applicable. Match the schedule to customer subscriptions, suppliers and operational services. The agreement SHOULD identify the customer and vendor contracts to be assigned. The schedule covers relevant amendments and orders and is not presumed to include every business contract. Drafting context.

sources.title: OW Holdings–Sitestar asset purchase agreement (2007), vendor contracts
sources.proposition: The Sitestar agreement listed on Schedule 5.16(a) the telecommunications circuit and service contracts to be assumed or executed by the buyer.
sources.verbatimQuote: Schedule 5.16(a) is complete list of all telecommunications circuit and service contracts to be assumed or executed by Buyer.

sources.title: ECOtality–Blink Acquisition asset purchase agreement (2013), assumed contracts
sources.proposition: The ECOtality agreement defined its assumed contracts as those identified on Schedule 2.01(a) or designated in writing by the buyer before a stated deadline.
sources.verbatimQuote: “Assumed Contracts” means (a) those Contracts primarily related to the Blink Business that are (i) identified on Schedule 2.01(a) hereto as Assumed Contracts and (ii) otherwise identified in writing to Sellers by the Buyer as Assumed Contracts prior to the Closing Date, and (b) those Undesignated Contracts identified in writing to the Sellers by Buyer as Assumed Contracts prior to the Assumed Contract Deadline.

sources.title: Jennifer M. Settles: Third-party consents
sources.citation: Jennifer M. Settles, Third-Party Consents, Law Office of Jennifer M. Settles (Apr. 25, 2025).
sources.proposition: Jennifer M. Settles explains that anti-assignment clauses require third-party consent before the buyer can assume the contract.
sources.verbatimQuote: These “anti-assignment clauses” trigger the need for a third-party consent before the Buyer can assume the contract.

requirements.requirementGuidance: Only if customer or vendor contracts are involved or platform accounts are involved, review the following safeguard. Otherwise mark it not applicable. Trace each consent dependency to an owner and evidence of approval or unresolved status. The agreement SHOULD identify required third-party consents and who is responsible for obtaining them. Consent effort standard, expense allocation and deadlines are negotiated. Drafting context.

sources.title: Luna–Micron asset purchase agreement (2018), consents representation
sources.proposition: The Luna seller represented that, except as set forth in Schedule 3.2(c), it was not required to give notice to or obtain consent from any person for the transaction.
sources.verbatimQuote: (c) Except as set forth in Schedule 3.2(c), Seller is not required to give any notice to or obtain any Consent from any Person in connection with the execution and delivery of this Agreement or the consummation or performance of any of the Contemplated Transactions.

sources.title: Greenfield Online–Dohring asset purchase agreement (2004), required consents
sources.proposition: The Greenfield Online seller represented that, except as set forth in Schedule 3.10, it was not party to any contract requiring counterparty consent to the transaction.
sources.verbatimQuote: Except as set forth in Schedule 3.10, Seller is not party to any contract or agreement that would require consent from the counterparty thereto to any of the transactions contemplated hereby.

sources.title: Luna–Micron asset purchase agreement (2018), required approvals
sources.proposition: The Luna agreement required the seller to use best efforts to obtain all material consents.
sources.verbatimQuote: Seller shall use Best Efforts to obtain all Material Consents.

requirements.requirementGuidance: Only if customer or vendor contracts are involved or platform accounts are involved, review the following safeguard. Otherwise mark it not applicable. Locate a consequence tied to the affected asset or contract, not only a general cooperation promise. The agreement SHOULD specify the consequence if a material transfer or consent remains unavailable at closing. Delay, exclusion, adjustment, termination or a permitted interim arrangement are alternatives; no default selected. Drafting context.

sources.title: Salem Web Network–Gloo asset purchase agreement (2023), contracts awaiting consent
sources.proposition: The Salem agreement treated a contract lacking consent at closing as not assigned until consent, with the seller passing its benefits to the buyer and the buyer paying the corresponding liabilities.
sources.verbatimQuote: In the event of a consent required with respect to the assignment of an Assumed Contract that has not been obtained before the Closing, then such Assumed Contract will be deemed not assigned until such consent shall have been obtained and, following the Closing Seller shall provide Buyer with the benefits of any such Assumed Contract until such consent is obtained, provided that Buyer shall undertake to pay or satisfy the corresponding liabilities for the enjoyment of such benefits to the extent Buyer would have been responsible therefor if such consent had been obtained and such Assumed Contract assigned and assumed by Buyer as of the Closing Date.

sources.title: Jennifer M. Settles: Third-party consents, consent escrow
sources.citation: Jennifer M. Settles, Third-Party Consents, Law Office of Jennifer M. Settles (Apr. 25, 2025).
sources.proposition: Jennifer M. Settles describes escrowing part of the purchase proceeds at closing pending receipt of necessary consents.
sources.verbatimQuote: One approach can involve the escrow of a portion of the purchase proceeds at closing, pending receipt of the necessary consents.

requirements.requirementGuidance: Reconcile the stated price with cash, noncash, deferred and contingent components. The agreement SHOULD state the consideration and when and how each component is payable. No financing mix or payment split is presumed. Drafting context.

sources.title: Mentor Graphics–SofTech asset purchase agreement (2013), holdback
sources.proposition: The SofTech agreement held back $320,000 of the closing price for twelve months, subject to reduction under its indemnity article.
sources.verbatimQuote: The US$320,000 balance of the Closing Purchase Price (“Holdback”) shall be payable to Seller, subject to possible reduction or deferred payment under Article V of this Agreement, by wire transfer twelve months after the Closing Date (“Holdback Period”).

sources.title: Innovative Gourmet–iGourmet asset purchase agreement (2024), post-closing payment
sources.proposition: The iGourmet agreement deferred $175,000 of its price to thirty days after closing.
sources.verbatimQuote: (ii) On the date that is thirty calendar days after the Closing, $175,000 (the “ Post-Closing Payment ”) by wire of immediately available funds to the Seller Account.

sources.title: Imke Ratschko: The Basics of an Asset Purchase Agreement, installments
sources.citation: Imke Ratschko, The Basics of an Asset Purchase Agreement, Ratschko PLLC (July 25, 2022; updated July 28, 2022).
sources.proposition: Imke Ratschko describes installment payments documented by a buyer promissory note, possibly secured by the purchased assets.
sources.verbatimQuote: If there are installments, the purchaser would usually give a promissory note for that amount and may give a security interest in the purchased assets, in case the purchaser defaults under the promissory note.

requirements.requirementGuidance: Identify an affirmative election; omission is not a defect for this optional feature. The agreement MAY include a post-closing purchase-price adjustment. Fixed price and adjustment are legitimate alternatives. Drafting context.

sources.title: Schwabe, Williamson & Wyatt: Getting the purchase price right, purpose of adjustments
sources.citation: Schwabe, Williamson & Wyatt, Getting the Purchase Price Right: Earn-outs, Escrows, and Post-Closing Adjustments in M&A Transactions (Nov. 22, 2016).
sources.proposition: Schwabe describes post-closing adjustments as increases or reductions to the price to account for changes in the company's financial condition between signing and closing.
sources.verbatimQuote: Finally, post-closing adjustments to the purchase price are increases or reductions to the purchase price to account for changes in the company’s financial condition between signing and closing.

requirements.requirementGuidance: Only if a price adjustment is elected, review the following safeguard. Otherwise mark it not applicable. Recalculate a worked example using the stated inputs and prevent double counting. The agreement SHOULD define the adjustment formula and accounting conventions. Working capital, inventory, cash or debt measures are not universal requirements. Drafting context.

sources.title: Schwabe, Williamson & Wyatt: Getting the purchase price right, accounting principles
sources.citation: Schwabe, Williamson & Wyatt, Getting the Purchase Price Right: Earn-outs, Escrows, and Post-Closing Adjustments in M&A Transactions (Nov. 22, 2016).
sources.proposition: Schwabe advises that post-closing adjustment provisions specify the accounting principles that will apply.
sources.verbatimQuote: In drafting the post-closing adjustment provisions, the parties should specify what accounting principles will apply.

sources.title: Luna–Micron asset purchase agreement (2018), net working capital
sources.proposition: The Luna agreement defined net working capital as the seller's receivables, inventory, prepaid expenses and other current assets, other than excluded assets, less current liabilities and excluding retained liabilities.
sources.verbatimQuote: “Net Working Capital” means, as of the Closing, (a) the sum of accounts receivable, Inventory and prepaid expenses and other current assets of the Seller, other than any Excluded Assets, less (b) Current Liabilities and excluding any Retained Liabilities.

requirements.requirementGuidance: Only if a price adjustment is elected, review the following safeguard. Otherwise mark it not applicable. Locate delivery deadline, access to records, objection process and decision endpoint. The agreement SHOULD specify how adjustment statements are reviewed and disputed. Expert determination and litigation/arbitration routes require deliberate coordination. Drafting context.

sources.title: Barlow & Williams: Purchase price adjustments, procedures
sources.proposition: Barlow & Williams recommend specifying the procedures for determining a price adjustment as precisely as possible to mitigate the risk of a dispute.
sources.verbatimQuote: To mitigate this risk, the parties should be as specific as possible in detailing the procedures to determine any purchase price adjustment.

sources.title: Barlow & Williams: Purchase price adjustments, review period
sources.proposition: Barlow & Williams describe a seller review period for the closing statement, commonly 30 days and possibly shorter in smaller transactions.
sources.verbatimQuote: After the closing statement is sent to the seller, the seller will have a period of time (30 days is common but this could be less in smaller transactions) to review it.

requirements.requirementGuidance: Identify the contingent-price election; absence is not a failure. The agreement MAY make part of the price contingent on post-closing performance. No earnout amount, period or metric is preselected. Drafting context.

sources.title: Schwabe, Williamson & Wyatt: Getting the purchase price right, earn-outs
sources.citation: Schwabe, Williamson & Wyatt, Getting the Purchase Price Right: Earn-outs, Escrows, and Post-Closing Adjustments in M&A Transactions (Nov. 22, 2016).
sources.proposition: Schwabe describes earn-outs as providing upward adjustment based on the company's post-closing performance.
sources.verbatimQuote: Earn-outs provide for upward adjustment based on positive performance by the company post-closing.

requirements.requirementGuidance: Only if an earnout is elected, review the following safeguard. Otherwise mark it not applicable. Compute a synthetic period from the definition, including inclusions and exclusions. The agreement SHOULD define the earnout metric, measurement period and calculation method. Caps, floors and acceleration are choices. Drafting context.

sources.title: Andrew J. Schultheis and Dylan Lowe: Earnouts (Davis Wright Tremaine), accounting definitions
sources.citation: Andrew J. Schultheis and Dylan Lowe, Earnouts in Mergers and Acquisitions Deals, Davis Wright Tremaine (June 2026).
sources.proposition: Andrew J. Schultheis and Dylan Lowe advise that an earnout provision clearly define the accounting standards, measurement periods and any inclusions or exclusions from the calculation.
sources.verbatimQuote: Regardless of which metric or milestone is chosen, the earnout provision should clearly define the applicable accounting standards (e.g., GAAP applied consistently with the target company's historical practices), the measurement periods, and any specific inclusions or exclusions from the calculation.

requirements.requirementGuidance: Only if an earnout is elected, review the following safeguard. Otherwise mark it not applicable. Locate express commitments or an express no-commitment position and evaluate metric interaction. The agreement SHOULD state the operating commitments, if any, that apply during the earnout period. This criterion does not call for an express duty to maximize the earnout. Drafting context.

sources.title: Andrew J. Schultheis and Dylan Lowe: Earnouts (Davis Wright Tremaine), operating covenant
sources.citation: Andrew J. Schultheis and Dylan Lowe, Earnouts in Mergers and Acquisitions Deals, Davis Wright Tremaine (June 2026).
sources.proposition: Andrew J. Schultheis and Dylan Lowe recommend that sellers seek at least an ordinary-course operating covenant.
sources.verbatimQuote: At a minimum, sellers should seek a covenant requiring the buyer to operate the business in the ordinary course consistent with past practices.

requirements.requirementGuidance: Only if an earnout is elected, review the following safeguard. Otherwise mark it not applicable. Locate reporting, supporting-record access, objection deadline and resolution mechanism. The agreement SHOULD specify the seller's process for reviewing and disputing earnout calculations. Access, confidentiality and independent review are tailored to the deal. Drafting context.

sources.title: Andrew J. Schultheis and Dylan Lowe: Earnouts (Davis Wright Tremaine), four areas
sources.citation: Andrew J. Schultheis and Dylan Lowe, Earnouts in Mergers and Acquisitions Deals, Davis Wright Tremaine (June 2026).
sources.proposition: Andrew J. Schultheis and Dylan Lowe say a well-drafted earnout provision addresses how performance is measured, how payments are made, how the seller's interests are protected and how disputes are resolved.
sources.verbatimQuote: A well-drafted earnout provision should address four key areas: how performance is measured, how payments are made, how the seller's interests are protected during the earnout period, and how disputes are resolved.

sources.title: Bankrate asset purchase agreement (2016)
sources.proposition: The Bankrate agreement supports access to the identified records and personnel to verify its earnout calculation.
sources.verbatimQuote: Upon receipt of an Earnout Statement, Seller and its accountants will be given reasonable access upon reasonable notice to Buyer’s relevant books, records, workpapers and personnel during business hours for the purpose of verifying the Earnout Adjusted EBITDA and Reference Adjusted EBITDA and the resulting Earnout Amount.

requirements.requirementGuidance: Identify whether either mechanism is elected; absence is not a failure. The agreement MAY reserve part of the price in escrow or as a holdback. Escrow and buyer-held amounts have different custody risks. Drafting context.

sources.title: Wright Lewis: Earnouts, escrows and holdbacks (Dunlap Bennett & Ludwig), escrow defined
sources.citation: Wright Lewis, Earnouts, Escrows, and Holdbacks, Dunlap Bennett & Ludwig (May 23, 2024).
sources.proposition: Wright Lewis describes an escrow as part of the price held by a third party, usually a bank or a law firm, until contractual obligations are met or as security for the seller's representations and warranties.
sources.verbatimQuote: An escrow is where part of the purchase price is held by a third party (usually a bank or a law firm) until certain contractual obligations are met, or as security for the seller’s representations and warranties.

sources.title: Mentor Graphics–SofTech asset purchase agreement (2013), holdback
sources.proposition: The SofTech agreement held back $320,000 of the closing price for twelve months, subject to reduction under its indemnity article.
sources.verbatimQuote: The US$320,000 balance of the Closing Purchase Price (“Holdback”) shall be payable to Seller, subject to possible reduction or deferred payment under Article V of this Agreement, by wire transfer twelve months after the Closing Date (“Holdback Period”).

requirements.requirementGuidance: Only if a purchase-price escrow or holdback is elected, review the following safeguard. Otherwise mark it not applicable. Trace an undisputed release and a disputed claim through the mechanism. The agreement SHOULD define the amount reserved and the conditions and timing for its release. Custodian, interest, fees and permitted deductions remain negotiated. Drafting context.

sources.title: Schwabe, Williamson & Wyatt: Getting the purchase price right, holdback amount
sources.citation: Schwabe, Williamson & Wyatt, Getting the Purchase Price Right: Earn-outs, Escrows, and Post-Closing Adjustments in M&A Transactions (Nov. 22, 2016).
sources.proposition: Schwabe explains that the holdback amount is usually based on a percentage of the price but may be increased for a specific known risk of an indemnity claim.
sources.verbatimQuote: The first consideration for an indemnity holdback is determining the amount. This is usually based on a percentage of the purchase price, but the amount may be increased if there is a specific known risk of an indemnity claim.

sources.title: Schwabe, Williamson & Wyatt: Getting the purchase price right
sources.citation: Schwabe, Williamson & Wyatt, Getting the Purchase Price Right: Earn-outs, Escrows, and Post-Closing Adjustments in M&A Transactions (Nov. 22, 2016).
sources.proposition: Schwabe explains that the holdback period largely depends on the survival periods for indemnity claims.
sources.verbatimQuote: The length of the holdback period will depend largely on the length of the survival periods for the indemnity claims.

sources.title: Wright Lewis: Earnouts, escrows and holdbacks (Dunlap Bennett & Ludwig), release in installments
sources.citation: Wright Lewis, Earnouts, Escrows, and Holdbacks, Dunlap Bennett & Ludwig (May 23, 2024).
sources.proposition: Wright Lewis suggests that a seller may negotiate release of an escrow or holdback in stages.
sources.verbatimQuote: It may be beneficial for a seller to negotiate a graduated release schedule, where a percentage of the escrow or holdback will be released to the seller at multiple intervals throughout the escrow or holdback period.

requirements.requirementGuidance: Identify the taxpayer-cost allocation and any contractual reimbursement duty. The agreement SHOULD specify which party bears transaction taxes. Jurisdiction and tax treatment need transaction-specific review; no default chosen. Drafting context.

sources.title: Greenfield Online–Dohring asset purchase agreement (2004), transfer taxes
sources.proposition: The Greenfield Online agreement made the buyer bear all sales, value added, use, transfer, registration, stamp and similar taxes imposed in connection with the sale of the transferred assets.
sources.verbatimQuote: (a) All sales, value added, use, transfer, registration, stamp and similar Taxes imposed in connection with the sale of the Transferred Assets shall be borne by Buyer.

sources.title: Grove–VitaMedica asset purchase agreement (2021), transfer taxes
sources.proposition: The Grove agreement split sales, use, transfer and similar taxes on the sale of the acquired assets equally between the seller and the buyer.
sources.verbatimQuote: Any United States or federal, state or local, sales, use, transfer, transfer gains or similar Taxes payable in connection with the sale and purchase of the Acquired Assets shall be paid equally by Seller and Buyer (i.e., each shall pay 50%).

requirements.requirementGuidance: Identify the allocation preparation, review, timing and disagreement process. The agreement SHOULD specify a process for coordinating purchase-price allocation reporting. Jurisdiction and tax treatment need transaction-specific review; no default chosen. Drafting context.

sources.title: OW Holdings–Sitestar asset purchase agreement (2007), consistent tax reporting
sources.proposition: The Sitestar agreement required each party to file its tax returns on the basis of the agreed allocation, barred inconsistent return positions and required each party to use the allocation as the basis for its Form 8594.
sources.verbatimQuote: Each Party shall file its respective income tax returns on the basis of the allocations agreed upon , and no Party shall thereafter take a return position inconsistent with such allocation. Each Party shall fully comply with the reporting requirements of Section 1060 of the Code relating to allocation rules for certain asset acquisitions, and will use this allocation as the basis for completing IRS Form 8594, which the Parties shall each file with the IRS on a timely basis.

sources.title: AMBREW–American Brewing asset purchase agreement (2015), allocation schedule
sources.proposition: The American Brewing agreement allocated the purchase price among the purchased assets for tax and accounting purposes as shown on an allocation schedule the buyer prepared before closing in accordance with IRS pronouncements.
sources.verbatimQuote: Seller and Buyer agree that the Purchase Price shall be allocated among the Purchased Assets for all purposes (including Tax and financial accounting) as shown on an allocation schedule (the " Allocation Schedule ") to be prepared by Buyer prior to the Closing Date in accordance with IRS pronouncements.

requirements.requirementGuidance: Check party capacity and approvals against the promised obligations. The agreement SHOULD include each party's statement of authority to enter and perform the transaction. Scope differs for entities and individuals. Drafting context.

sources.title: Innovative Gourmet–iGourmet asset purchase agreement (2024), seller authority
sources.proposition: The iGourmet seller represented that it had the power and authority to enter into the agreement and the other transaction documents and to carry out the transaction.
sources.verbatimQuote: Seller has all necessary limited liability company power and authority to enter into this Agreement and the other Transaction Documents to which Seller is a party, to carry out its obligations hereunder and thereunder, and to consummate the transactions contemplated hereby and thereby.

sources.title: Bankrate asset purchase agreement (2016), owner authority
sources.proposition: The Bankrate agreement included a representation that the owner had the power and authority to execute, deliver and perform the agreement and its other transaction documents.
sources.verbatimQuote: Owner has all requisite power and authority to execute, deliver and perform its obligations under this Agreement and each of the Transaction Documents to which it is a party.

requirements.requirementGuidance: Locate title statement, disclosed encumbrances and any release commitments. The agreement SHOULD state the seller's ownership and lien position for the purchased assets. Permitted encumbrances and lien-release conditions are negotiated. Drafting context.

sources.title: Salem asset purchase agreement (2023), title to sale assets
sources.proposition: The Salem agreement represented that the seller had good, valid and marketable title to all of the sale assets, free and clear of any liens except permitted liens.
sources.verbatimQuote: Seller has good, valid and marketable title to all of the Sale Assets, free and clear of any Liens except for Permitted Liens.

sources.title: Margaret M. Salinas: Five issues to address when acquiring a business, lien payoff
sources.citation: Margaret M. Salinas, Five Issues to Address When Acquiring a Business, Chuhak & Tecson (Apr. 18, 2024).
sources.proposition: Margaret M. Salinas recommends making payoff of existing liens and evidence of their release a condition precedent to closing.
sources.verbatimQuote: If the seller(s) have existing liens, it should be a condition precedent to closing that those liens are paid off and evidence of the release of such liens is provided to the purchaser.

requirements.requirementGuidance: Locate dispute scope and disclosure record; distinguish actual knowledge from absolute assurance. The agreement SHOULD require disclosure of material pending or threatened disputes affecting the transferred business. Knowledge, materiality and lookback are choices. Drafting context.

sources.title: Salem asset purchase agreement (2023), litigation representation
sources.proposition: The Salem seller represented that, except as listed on Schedule 3.8, no claims, investigations or other proceedings relating to the business were pending or, to its knowledge, threatened against it.
sources.verbatimQuote: Except as otherwise provided in Schedule 3.8, there are no claims, investigations, or administrative proceedings, arbitrations, or other proceedings pending or, to Seller’s knowledge, threatened against Seller relating to the Business.
sources.pullQuoteLocator: Except as otherwise provided in Schedule|Seller relating to the Business.

sources.title: Greenfield Online–Dohring asset purchase agreement (2004), litigation representation
sources.proposition: The Greenfield Online seller represented that no proceedings were pending or, to its knowledge, threatened against the seller, the business or the transferred assets, and that no orders affected them.
sources.verbatimQuote: There are no (i) actions, suits, claims, hearings, arbitrations, proceedings (public or private) or governmental investigations that have been brought by or against any Governmental Authority or any other Person (collectively, “Proceedings”) pending or, to the knowledge of Seller, threatened, against or by Seller, the Business or any of the Transferred Assets or which seek to enjoin or rescind the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, nor, to the knowledge of Seller, is there any valid basis for any such Proceedings; and (ii) existing orders, judgments or decrees of any Governmental Authority naming Seller as an affected party affecting any of the Transferred Assets, the Business or the performance by Seller of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, nor, to the knowledge of Seller, is there any valid basis for any such Proceedings.

requirements.requirementGuidance: Trace each exception to the representation it qualifies. The agreement SHOULD link exceptions to representations to identifiable disclosure-schedule entries. If cross-disclosure is used, its effect is stated. Drafting context.

sources.title: Tyler Conway and Tracy Belton: Tips on drafting and negotiating disclosure schedules (Arnold & Porter)
sources.citation: Tyler Conway and Tracy Belton, Tips on Drafting and Negotiating Disclosure Schedules, Arnold & Porter (Dec. 4, 2015).
sources.proposition: Tyler Conway and Tracy Belton identify two categories of disclosure-schedule information: lists and exceptions.
sources.verbatimQuote: There are two categories of information presented in disclosure schedules: lists and exceptions.

sources.title: Conor Meyers: Representations and warranties in a business sale, scheduled exceptions
sources.citation: Conor Meyers, Reps and Warranties in a Business Sale, Clark Meyers (Aug. 21, 2026).
sources.proposition: Conor Meyers explains that a properly scheduled exception is not a breach of the representation.
sources.verbatimQuote: A representation is made except as disclosed, so an exception properly scheduled is not a breach at all.

sources.title: Luna–Micron asset purchase agreement (2018), consents schedule
sources.proposition: The Luna agreement's representation that no notice or consent is needed for the transaction is qualified by the consents listed on Schedule 3.2(c).
sources.verbatimQuote: Except as set forth in Schedule 3.2(c), Seller is not required to give any notice to or obtain any Consent from any Person in connection with the execution and delivery of this Agreement or the consummation or performance of any of the Contemplated Transactions.
sources.pullQuoteLocator: Except as set forth in Schedule 3.2(c),|any of the Contemplated Transactions.

requirements.requirementGuidance: Only if signing precedes closing, review the following safeguard. Otherwise mark it not applicable. Locate commitments addressing material changes to the business being acquired. The agreement SHOULD specify the seller's operating commitments between signing and closing. Ordinary-course standard, exceptions and purchaser-consent process require negotiation. Drafting context.

sources.title: Greenfield Online–Dohring asset purchase agreement (2004), conduct of the business
sources.proposition: The Greenfield Online agreement required the seller, until closing, to conduct the business in the ordinary course, preserve the transferred assets and use commercially appropriate efforts to preserve the business's goodwill with third parties.
sources.verbatimQuote: From the date hereof until the Closing Date, Seller shall conduct the Business in the ordinary course and shall preserve intact the Transferred Assets, and shall use its commercially appropriate efforts to preserve intact the Business’s goodwill with third parties.

sources.title: Bankrate–NextAdvisor asset purchase agreement (2016), conduct before closing
sources.proposition: The Bankrate agreement required the seller, before closing, to operate in the ordinary course, preserve its organization and assets, keep its workforce available and preserve key business relationships.
sources.verbatimQuote: During the period from the date of this Agreement until the earlier of (x) the Closing or (y) the date this Agreement is terminated in accordance with its terms (such period, the “Pre-Closing Period”), Seller shall, and Owner shall cause Seller to, (i) operate the Business only in the ordinary course of business consistent with past practice, (ii) use its commercially reasonable efforts to preserve substantially intact its business organization and assets; (iii) use its commercially reasonable efforts to keep available the services of its employees and independent contractors; (iv) use its commercially reasonable efforts to preserve Seller’s relationships with customers, suppliers and other Persons with which Seller has significant business relationships; (v) pay all Indebtedness, Taxes and other obligations in the ordinary course of business and (vi) keep and maintain Seller’s assets and properties in good repair and normal operating condition, ordinary wear and tear excepted.

requirements.requirementGuidance: Trace payment and conveyance sequencing to a defined closing event. The agreement SHOULD state the closing process and the event at which the parties exchange performance. Simultaneous exchange, escrow closing and transfers in stages are alternatives. Drafting context.

sources.title: Grove–VitaMedica asset purchase agreement (2021), simultaneous closing
sources.proposition: The Grove agreement held its closing simultaneously with the execution and delivery of the agreement.
sources.verbatimQuote: Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, the closing of the purchase, sale and transactions contemplated by this Agreement (the “Closing”) shall be held simultaneously with the execution and delivery of this Agreement, which is the date of this Agreement first above set forth.
sources.pullQuoteLocator: Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, the|Agreement first above set forth.

sources.title: Luna–Micron asset purchase agreement (2018), closing payments
sources.proposition: The Luna agreement required the buyer at closing to wire the purchase price less the escrow amount to the seller and to wire the escrow amount to the escrow agent.
sources.verbatimQuote: In addition to any other documents or deliverables to be delivered under other provisions of this Agreement, at the Closing: (a) Buyer shall pay or cause to be paid, in cash by wire transfer of immediately available funds to an account designated in writing by Seller to Buyer, the Purchase Price less the Escrow Amount; (b) Buyer shall deliver the Escrow Amount, in cash by wire transfer of immediately available funds, to the Escrow Agent, to be held and disbursed by the Escrow Agent in accordance with the terms of this Agreement and the Escrow Agreement;

requirements.requirementGuidance: Only if signing precedes closing, review the following safeguard. Otherwise mark it not applicable. Match each condition to the entitled party, satisfaction evidence and waiver process. The agreement SHOULD identify the conditions to each party's obligation to close. Financing, material adverse change and diligence conditions are not automatic. Drafting context.

sources.title: Greenfield Online–Dohring asset purchase agreement (2004), buyer closing conditions
sources.proposition: The Greenfield Online agreement conditioned the buyer's obligation to close on receiving all of the seller's closing deliveries and on the accuracy of the seller's representations.
sources.verbatimQuote: The obligations of Buyer to consummate the Closing are subject to the satisfaction of each of the following conditions (any of which may be waived by Buyer, in whole or in part): (a) Buyer shall have received all of the deliveries from Seller required pursuant to Sections 2.5 hereof; -18- (b) The representations and warranties made by Seller pursuant to Section 3 shall be true and correct in all material respects (except for such representations and warranties as are already qualified by materiality concepts, which shall be true and correct as of the Closing Date) on and as of the Closing Date as though made on and as of the Closing Date or, in the case of representations and warranties made as of a specified date earlier than the Closing Date, on and as of such earlier date;

sources.title: Luna–Micron asset purchase agreement (2018)
sources.proposition: The Luna agreement supports treating its material consents as closing conditions.
sources.verbatimQuote: Each of the Material Consents shall have been obtained and shall be in full force and effect.

requirements.requirementGuidance: Reconcile the deliverable list with transfer instruments, approvals, releases and payment documents actually required by the deal. The agreement SHOULD identify each closing deliverable and the party responsible for providing it. A deliverable is conditional on the corresponding asset, liability or election. Drafting context.

sources.title: Luna–Micron asset purchase agreement (2018), seller closing deliveries
sources.proposition: The Luna agreement required the seller to deliver at closing a bill of sale for tangible personal property and an assignment and assumption agreement for intangible assets.
sources.verbatimQuote: (c) Seller shall deliver or cause to be delivered to Buyer the following items (in form and substance reasonably satisfactory to Buyer and its counsel, unless otherwise specified below): (i) a bill of sale for all of the Purchased Assets that are Tangible Personal Property in substantially the form of Exhibit B (the “Bill of Sale”), duly executed by Seller; (ii) an assignment of all of the Purchased Assets that are intangible personal property in substantially the form of Exhibit C, which assignment shall also contain Buyer’s undertaking and assumption of the Assumed Liabilities (the “Assignment and Assumption Agreement”), duly executed by Seller;

sources.title: Grove–VitaMedica asset purchase agreement (2021), IP and domain assignments
sources.proposition: The Grove agreement required the seller to deliver at closing assignments of patents, trademarks and copyrights and a domain name assignment, among other documents.
sources.verbatimQuote: (ii) An Assignment of Patents, Assignment of Servicemarks and Trademarks and Assignment of Copyrights in the form of Exhibits F-1, F-2 and F-3 executed by Seller; and (iii) Non-Competition Agreements in the form of Exhibit G (the "Selling Parties’ Non-Competition Agreements") executed by each of the Selling Parties; and (iv) Employment Agreements in the form of Exhibits H-1 and H-2 executed by each of the Seller Stockholders (“the Employment Agreements”) Page 6 (v) An opinion from Seller’s legal counsel in form and substance as set forth in Exhibit I attached hereto, addressed to the Buyer; and (vi) A certificate executed by the President of Seller certifying that such President has the power and authority to enter into on behalf of Seller this Agreement and the other documents to be executed by Seller pursuant hereto, and to bind Seller hereto and thereto; and (vii) A Domain Name Assignment in the form of Exhibit J executed by Seller;

sources.title: Chefs' Warehouse–Allen Brothers asset purchase agreement (2013), closing deliverables
sources.proposition: The Chefs' Warehouse agreement required the seller parties to deliver at closing a signed closing statement setting forth the flow of funds, and the signed escrow agreements.
sources.verbatimQuote: At the Closing, the Seller Parties shall deliver to Buyer, in addition to any other documents to be delivered under the provisions of this Agreement, all of the following documents: (i) the Closing Statement, dated as of the date hereof, setting forth the flow of funds for the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, duly executed by each of the Seller Parties (the “Closing Statement”); (ii) the Escrow Agreement A and the Escrow Agreement B, duly executed by the Seller and its Subsidiaries and the Shareholder, as applicable;

requirements.requirementGuidance: Identify the election; no support obligation is inferred from silence. The agreement MAY require the seller to provide post-closing transition services. No fixed hours, term or fee is presumed. Drafting context.

sources.title: Venn Law Group: Transition and consulting agreements
sources.citation: Venn Law Group, Transition Consulting Agreements (Nov. 27, 2024).
sources.proposition: Venn Law Group describes transition agreements typically running three to twelve months, longer for complex businesses.
sources.verbatimQuote: The term, or duration, of a transition agreement is a fundamental element typically ranging from three to twelve months, although it can extend longer if the business is more complex.

requirements.requirementGuidance: Only if transition support is elected, review the following safeguard. Otherwise mark it not applicable. Locate deliverables, service boundaries, end date and payment rule. The agreement SHOULD specify the tasks, duration and compensation for transition services. Named personnel appear only where agreed and available. Drafting context.

sources.title: Venn Law Group: Transition and consulting agreements, structure
sources.citation: Venn Law Group, Transition Consulting Agreements (Nov. 27, 2024).
sources.proposition: Venn Law Group describes terms for transition duration, weekly hours and compensation as giving the seller's knowledge transfer a structured approach.
sources.verbatimQuote: By setting terms for the transition duration, weekly hours, and clear compensation, transition agreements provide a structured approach for the seller to share essential knowledge while helping the buyer feel prepared to take over.

sources.title: Venn Law Group: Transition and consulting agreements, compensation
sources.citation: Venn Law Group, Transition Consulting Agreements (Nov. 27, 2024).
sources.proposition: Venn Law Group observes that sellers are usually paid hourly or monthly for transition services.
sources.verbatimQuote: In exchange for their time and expertise, the seller is usually compensated on an hourly or fixed monthly basis.

requirements.requirementGuidance: Locate limits, expense responsibility and an endpoint or objective completion standard. The agreement SHOULD specify reasonable post-closing cooperation to complete agreed transfers. This does not substitute for required third-party permission. Drafting context.

sources.title: Bankrate asset purchase agreement (2016), further assurances
sources.proposition: The Bankrate further-assurances clause required each party to execute further instruments and take additional action reasonably requested to effect, consummate, confirm or evidence the transfer of the purchased assets.
sources.verbatimQuote: Each of the Parties shall execute and deliver such further instruments of conveyance and transfer and take such additional action as the other may reasonably request to effect, consummate, confirm or evidence the transfer to Buyer of the Purchased Assets, the assumption by Buyer of the Assumed Liabilities and the conduct by Buyer of the Business, and shall execute such documents as may be necessary to assist Buyer in preserving or perfecting its rights in the Purchased Assets and its ability to conduct the Business.

sources.title: Grove–VitaMedica asset purchase agreement (2021), further assurances
sources.proposition: The Grove agreement required the selling parties, after closing and at the buyer's request, to deliver further transfer instruments needed to vest title in the buyer.
sources.verbatimQuote: Following the Closing Date, at the request of the Buyer, the Selling Parties shall deliver any further instruments of transfer and shall take all such further action as may be necessary or appropriate to vest in the Buyer good title to the Acquired Assets that were to be transferred previously and to effectuate the transactions contemplated herein.

requirements.requirementGuidance: Only if signing precedes closing, review the following safeguard. Otherwise mark it not applicable. Trace outside date, breach and failed-condition scenarios to an eligible party and consequence. The agreement SHOULD identify termination rights and their consequences before closing. Cure periods, deposits and surviving duties are choices. Drafting context.

sources.title: Luna–Micron asset purchase agreement (2018), outside date
sources.proposition: The Luna agreement let the buyer or the seller terminate if the other's closing conditions would not be fulfilled by December 31, 2018, unless the terminating party's own failure to perform caused it.
sources.verbatimQuote: (c) by Buyer, if any of the conditions set forth in Article 7 shall not have been, or if it becomes apparent that any of such conditions will not be, fulfilled by December 31, 2018, unless such failure shall be due to the failure of Buyer to perform or comply with any of the covenants or agreements hereof to be performed or complied with by it prior to the Closing; (d) by Seller, if any of the conditions set forth in Article 8 shall not have been, or if it becomes apparent that any of such conditions will not be, fulfilled by December 31, 2018, unless such failure shall be due to the failure of Seller

sources.title: Bankrate asset purchase agreement (2016), effect of termination
sources.proposition: The Bankrate agreement provided that on termination it would have no further force and effect, except for listed surviving provisions and liability for earlier willful and material breach.
sources.verbatimQuote: In the event of termination of this Agreement as provided above, this Agreement shall immediately terminate and have no further force and effect and there shall be no Liability on the part of any Party to any other Party under this Agreement, except that (a) the covenants and agreements set forth in this Section 9.2 and Article 11 (Miscellaneous) and all definitions herein necessary to interpret any of the foregoing provisions shall remain in full force and effect and survive such termination indefinitely and (b) nothing in this Section 9.2 shall release any Party from any Liability for any willful and material breach by such Party of this Agreement before the effective date of such termination, or otherwise affect any of the rights or remedies available to any Party with respect to the breach of this Agreement by any Party before the effective date of such termination.

sources.title: ECOtality–Blink Acquisition asset purchase agreement (2013), termination grounds
sources.proposition: The ECOtality agreement's section 9.01(b) let the sellers terminate before closing if the buyer materially breached a representation or failed to perform its pre-closing covenants, and section 9.01(e) tied another termination right to a bankruptcy court approval order.
sources.verbatimQuote: This Agreement may be terminated at any time prior to the Closing: (a) by mutual written agreement of the Sellers and Buyer; (b) by the Sellers, if Buyer has breached any representation or warranty of Buyer contained in this Agreement in any material respect, or if Buyer shall fail to perform or comply in all material respects with all covenants and obligations of Buyer under this Agreement to be performed or complied with by it on or prior to the Closing Date; provided, that Sellers are not then in material breach of their representations, warranties, covenants or obligations under this Agreement; (c) by the Sellers, if any condition to the obligations of Sellers set forth in Section 6.01 (c) or (d) shall have become incapable of fulfillment; provided, that Sellers are not then in material breach of their representations, warranties, covenants or obligations under this Agreement; (d) by the Buyer, if any condition to the obligation of Buyer set forth in Section 6.02 shall have become incapable of fulfillment; provided, that Buyer is not then in material breach of its representations, warranties, covenants or obligations under this Agreement; (e) by either the Sellers or Buyer, if the Closing shall not have been consummated on or before the date that is two (2) Business Days after the entry of the Approval Order by the Bankruptcy Court, unless the party seeking termination is in material breach of its representations, warranties, covenants or obligations under this Agreement.

requirements.requirementGuidance: Identify election and covered subjects; absence is not a failure of this optional mechanism. The agreement MAY provide contractual indemnification for identified losses. Other contractual remedies require separate review; no universal indemnity is prescribed. Drafting context.

sources.title: Robbie Crosier: The indemnification clause in business acquisitions (Peters Kussmaul Crosier), negotiation
sources.citation: Robbie Crosier, Explanation of the Indemnification Clause in Business Acquisitions, Peters Kussmaul Crosier (June 23, 2025).
sources.proposition: Robbie Crosier describes the final indemnification clause as a product of negotiation reflecting each party's relative leverage.
sources.verbatimQuote: The final indemnification clause is a product of negotiation, reflecting the relative leverage of each party.

sources.title: Luna–Micron asset purchase agreement (2018), basket
sources.proposition: The Luna agreement made the seller liable for representation losses only after they exceeded a $50,000 basket, and then only for the excess.
sources.verbatimQuote: (a) Seller shall not be liable to the Buyer Indemnified Parties for indemnification under Section 11.2(a) until the aggregate amount of all Losses in respect of indemnification under Section 11.2(a) exceeds $50,000 (the “Basket”), in which event Seller shall only be required to pay or be liable for Losses in excess of the Basket.

requirements.requirementGuidance: Only if indemnification is elected, review the following safeguard. Otherwise mark it not applicable. Trace breach, assumed-liability and retained-liability examples to the correct indemnitor. The agreement SHOULD identify the indemnifying party, protected party and covered claim categories. Covered categories and exclusions remain negotiated. Drafting context.

sources.title: Smart Repair Pro–Beard Revive purchase agreement (2021; filed by Jeffs Brands in 2022), indemnification
sources.proposition: The Jeffs Brands agreement made the buyer indemnify the seller for the buyer's operation of the assets after the completed migration and the seller indemnify the buyer for the seller's operation before it.
sources.verbatimQuote: (a) Buyer agrees to indemnify Seller from all liabilities arising out of Buyer’s operation of the Assets after the Completed Migration; (b) Seller agrees to indemnify Buyer from all liabilities arising out of Seller’s operation of the Asset prior to the Completed Migration; and, (c) The Parties agree to indemnify Broker from and against any and all claims, demands, judgments, liabilities, costs, and fees, including attorney’s fees, arising out of or related to this Agreement, including but not limited to the Buyer or Seller’s breach of any provision of this Agreement.

sources.title: Greenfield Online–Dohring asset purchase agreement (2004), shareholder indemnity
sources.proposition: In Section 9.7 of the Greenfield Online agreement, the shareholder indemnified the buyer for breaches of two listed seller representations and for the seller's fraud, subject to stated limits.
sources.verbatimQuote: Shareholder shall indemnify and hold harmless the Buyer Indemnitees, subject to the limits set forth in Section 9.3, in respect of any and all Damages incurred by any Buyer Indemnitee in connection with, or resulting from, any or all of the following: (a) Any breach of the representations or warranties made by Seller pursuant to Sections 3.8 and 3.15 of this Agreement; and (b) Any fraudulent statement or representation of Seller contained in this Agreement, or supplied to Buyer by Seller in writing after the execution of this Agreement, where “fraudulent” means knowing, intentional fraud.

requirements.requirementGuidance: Only if indemnification is elected, review the following safeguard. Otherwise mark it not applicable. Locate notice, defense control, settlement consent and payment mechanics. The agreement SHOULD specify the procedure for direct and third-party indemnity claims. The effect of late notice is defined rather than assumed to be automatic forfeiture. Drafting context.

sources.title: Luna–Micron asset purchase agreement (2018), response to a direct claim
sources.proposition: The Luna agreement gave the indemnifying party 30 days after receiving notice of a direct claim to respond in writing.
sources.verbatimQuote: The Indemnifying Party shall have 30 days after its receipt of such notice to respond in writing to such Direct Claim.
sources.pullQuoteLocator: The Indemnifying Party shall have 30|writing to such Direct Claim.

sources.title: Salem asset purchase agreement (2023), third-party claims
sources.proposition: The Salem agreement required a party seeking indemnification to give the indemnifying party prompt written notice, in reasonable detail, of any third-party claim or suit.
sources.verbatimQuote: Any party seeking payment or indemnification under this Article IX (the “Indemnified Party”) shall give prompt notice in reasonable detail in writing to the party against whom indemnity is to be sought (the “Indemnifying Party”) of the assertion of any claim or the commencement of any suit, action or proceeding by any third party (“Third Party Claim”) in respect of which indemnity may be sought.

requirements.requirementGuidance: Trace a timely and a late claim separately for each claim category. The agreement SHOULD state any agreed survival periods or contractual claim deadlines. An express choice to impose no contractual deadline is assessable; counsel reviews legal limits. Drafting context.

sources.title: Luna–Micron asset purchase agreement (2018), survival
