sources.verbatimQuote: (a) The Amazon FBA account associated with the Business, including all associated accounts, content, data, customer lists, databases, files, and artwork; (b) The www.whoobli.com domain name and its associated domain name registration; (c) All accounts, content, data, customer lists, databases, files, and artwork associated with the Business; (d) All trademark and trade names and related goodwill associated with the Business and all copyright rights pursuant to 17 U.S.C. § 106 associated with the Business; (e) All licenses for applications or plugins used in connection with the Business; (f) All prepaid expenses and subscriptions as of the Effective Date of this Agreement associated with the Business; and, (g) All inventory associated with the business including in order, in transport, housed at in a 3rd party warehouse or currently housed at Amazon Fulfillment Centers (“Inventory”).

sources.title: Salem asset purchase agreement (2023), registrar transfer documentation
sources.proposition: The Salem agreement required the seller, promptly after closing, to provide the documentation or certifications the current registrar requires to transfer the domain names to the buyer.
sources.verbatimQuote: Promptly following the Closing, Seller shall provide a notarized assignment of all registered trademarks of Seller and all documentation or certifications required by the current registrar to Buyer of all of the Domain Names used in the Business (the “Post-Closing Transfer Items”).

sources.title: Transfer a Stripe account due to a business sale or acquisition (Stripe Support)
sources.proposition: Stripe tells an account owner transferring the account because of a business sale to contact Stripe Support first to confirm which information needs updating.
sources.verbatimQuote: If you are the existing owner of a Stripe account and you want to transfer ownership of your account to someone else, such as in the case of selling your business or having been acquired, you will first need to reach out to Stripe Support to confirm which information updates need to be made.

sources.title: Transfer apps, active accounts (Google Play Console Help)
sources.citation: Get your app ready to transfer; accessed October 3, 2026
sources.proposition: Google Play requires both the original and the target developer accounts to be registered and active before a transfer request can be submitted.
sources.verbatimQuote: Before you can submit a transfer request from your original account to a different account (known as your target account), both Google Play developer accounts need to be registered and active.

requirements.requirementGuidance: Only if data is included, review the following safeguard. Otherwise mark it not applicable. Trace dataset categories and locations to the purchased/excluded asset descriptions. The agreement SHOULD identify the datasets included in and excluded from the transfer. Customer, employee, analytics and payment-related data are treated separately where relevant. Drafting context.

sources.title: Salem asset purchase agreement (2023), customer records and seller copy
sources.proposition: The Salem agreement transferred originals or true and complete copies of its customer records, lists and databases, while allowing the seller to keep a copy for internal recordkeeping and other legal and accounting purposes.
sources.verbatimQuote: (g) Records. The originals (where available) or true and complete copies (if originals are not available) of all of the email subscriber/customer records, customer lists, customer contact information, registered user lists, databases, access codes, books, records, files, videos, logs and ledgers pertaining to the Sale Assets or used in the operation of the Business as set forth on Schedule 1.1(g) (collectively, “Records”); provided, that Seller may keep a copy of the Records for its internal recordkeeping and other legal and accounting purposes;

sources.title: Greenfield Online–Dohring asset purchase agreement (2004), deletion of overlapping panel members
sources.proposition: The Greenfield Online agreement required the seller to stop emailing overlapping panel members at closing, permanently delete them from its other panel within five days of closing and have an officer certify that in writing.
sources.verbatimQuote: Seller agrees that on the Closing Date it will stop sending, and will stop authorizing any other Person to send, any email messages via the YIO domain or otherwise to members of the YIO Panel that are also members of the Panel, and that within five days of the Closing Seller will permanently delete from the YIO panel all members that are also members of the Panel, and an officer of Seller shall so certify in writing to the Buyer.

requirements.requirementGuidance: Only if personal data is included, review the following safeguard. Otherwise mark it not applicable. Locate a review owner and a record addressing historical promises, intended uses and affected jurisdictions. The agreement SHOULD make completion of the personal-data transfer subject to an identified review of applicable notices, permissions and legal constraints. This is a review safeguard, not a finding that any particular consent is universally required. Drafting context.

sources.title: Greenfield Online–Dohring asset purchase agreement (2004), privacy policy
sources.proposition: The Greenfield Online agreement required the buyer after closing to use the transferred assets only in accordance with the seller’s posted privacy policy, unless it lawfully amended that policy.
sources.verbatimQuote: Prior to the Closing, Seller shall operate the Business in accordance with the privacy policy posted on Seller’s website on the date hereof, and after the Closing, Buyer shall use the Transferred Assets only in accordance with such privacy policy of Seller, provided however, that Buyer retains the right to amend such privacy policy and act in accordance with any such amended policy if and to the extent it implements any such amendment in accordance with all Laws.
sources.pullQuoteLocator: Prior to the Closing, Seller shall|in accordance with all Laws.

sources.title: Meta Financial–Fort Knox asset purchase agreement (2015), privacy and security
sources.proposition: The Meta Financial agreement included a representation that, except as scheduled, the companies had complied with privacy laws and their own policies on the collection, use, disclosure, protection and transfer of personal information.
sources.verbatimQuote: With respect to any Personal Information collected or processed by or on behalf of any Company, except as set forth on Schedule 4.23: (i) such Company and, to the Companies’ knowledge, such Company’s vendors and subcontractors (with respect to work performed on behalf of such Company) at all times have complied in all material respects with all applicable U.S., state and foreign Laws (“Privacy Laws”), standard industry practices and their own published, posted, and internal agreements and policies (which are in material compliance with applicable Privacy Laws) with respect to (A) the collection, use, disclosure, protection and transfer of Personal Information;

requirements.requirementGuidance: Only if data is included, review the following safeguard. Otherwise mark it not applicable. Locate authorized recipients, secure delivery method and confirmation of receipt. The agreement SHOULD specify the access and security controls for moving transferred data. Controls are proportionate to the data. Drafting context.

sources.title: Salem asset purchase agreement (2023), migration of content to buyer's servers
sources.proposition: The Salem agreement required the seller to cooperate in moving purchased files and content from the seller's servers to servers the buyer selected as soon as reasonably practicable after closing.
sources.verbatimQuote: Seller will cooperate with Buyer to transfer title to all of Seller’s files and content purchased by Buyer and stored at Closing on Seller’s servers from those servers to servers selected by Buyer as soon as reasonably practicable following the Closing.

sources.title: Meta Financial–Fort Knox asset purchase agreement (2015), data security controls
sources.proposition: The Meta Financial agreement included a representation that the companies used encryption of at least 128-bit strength and had a security plan identifying and controlling risks to personal information.
sources.verbatimQuote: Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, such Company (i) uses adequate-strength encryption technology of at least 128-bit and (ii) has implemented a comprehensive security plan that (A) identifies internal and external risks to the security of such Company’s confidential information and Personal Information and (B) implements, monitors and improves adequate and effective safeguards to control those risks.
sources.pullQuoteLocator: Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, such Company (i)|safeguards to control those risks.

Locate permitted retained copies, purposes and a deletion or retention endpoint. The agreement SHOULD allocate responsibility for data retained after closing, including the retention and deletion process. Counsel determines applicable retention duties; no universal deletion deadline is selected. Drafting context.

Locate scope, disclosure schedule and applicable qualification of the incident statement. The agreement SHOULD require disclosure of material known security incidents affecting the transferred business. Knowledge, materiality, lookback and remediation allocation are negotiated. Drafting context.

sources.title: Salem asset purchase agreement (2023), security incidents
sources.proposition: The Salem agreement included a knowledge-qualified representation that there had been no security incident involving third-party processors during the past five years.
sources.verbatimQuote: To Seller’s knowledge during the past five years there has been no Security Incident involving any Business System operated or controlled by any Third Party Processor or any Business Data under the custody or control of any Third Party Processor.

sources.title: Grove–VitaMedica asset purchase agreement (2021), data security incidents
sources.proposition: The Grove seller represented that it had not experienced any incident in which personal information or other sensitive data was or may have been stolen or improperly accessed.
sources.verbatimQuote: Seller has not experienced any incident in which personal information or other sensitive data was or may have been stolen or improperly accessed, acquired, destroyed, damaged, disclosed, corrupted, or altered, and Seller is not aware of any facts suggesting the likelihood of the foregoing, including without limitation, any breach of security or receipt of any notices or complaints from any Person regarding personal information or other data.

requirements.requirementGuidance: Distinguish gross/net receipts, periods, currency and recurring/nonrecurring items used in the deal. The agreement SHOULD define the revenue measures used to support the stated business economics. Accounting basis and adjustments are deal-specific. Drafting context.

sources.title: Grove–VitaMedica asset purchase agreement (2021), adjusted revenues definition
sources.proposition: The Grove agreement’s revenue-shortfall appendix defines adjusted revenues as gross revenues of the business, excluding revenue from sales of assets outside the ordinary course and repricing sales to the buyer’s affiliates at arm’s-length amounts.
sources.verbatimQuote: “Adjusted Revenues” – gross revenues of the Business, adjusted as follows: (a) exclude revenues of the Business from the sale of assets other than in the Ordinary Course of Business; (b) the purchase and sales prices of goods and services sold by the Business to Affiliates of Buyer, shall be adjusted to reflect the amounts that the Target would have received or paid if dealing with an independent party in an arm’s-length commercial transaction.

sources.title: Bankrate asset purchase agreement (2016), gross profit net of chargebacks
sources.citation: earnout definitions, Buyer Brand Gross Profit
sources.proposition: The Bankrate agreement defines a gross-profit measure as net revenue less bad debt and customer chargebacks and credits, minus traffic acquisition costs.
sources.verbatimQuote: “Buyer Brand Gross Profit” means (A) the net revenue directly generated by the Buyer Brand Business, less bad debt and customer chargebacks and credits minus the (B) traffic acquisition costs (including media, creative development and technology expenditures) of the net revenue directly generated by the Buyer Brand Business.

requirements.requirementGuidance: Trace a sample across sales, processor settlements and relevant accounting records, with explanations of differences. The agreement SHOULD provide a process for reconciling claimed revenue with underlying business records. Verification scope and confidentiality restrictions remain negotiable. Drafting context.

sources.title: Bankrate asset purchase agreement (2016)
sources.proposition: The Bankrate agreement supports access to the identified records and personnel to verify its earnout calculation.
sources.verbatimQuote: Upon receipt of an Earnout Statement, Seller and its accountants will be given reasonable access upon reasonable notice to Buyer’s relevant books, records, workpapers and personnel during business hours for the purpose of verifying the Earnout Adjusted EBITDA and Reference Adjusted EBITDA and the resulting Earnout Amount.

sources.title: Grove–VitaMedica asset purchase agreement (2021)
sources.proposition: The Grove agreement supports keeping separate business books during its revenue computation period.
sources.verbatimQuote: Buyer shall maintain separate accounting books and records for the Business during the Computation Period.

requirements.requirementGuidance: Only if prepaid customer obligations exist, review the following safeguard. Otherwise mark it not applicable. Trace prepaid subscriptions, credits or outstanding orders to the responsible performer. The agreement SHOULD allocate the cost of fulfilling customer obligations paid for before the cutoff. Performance allocation and any price credit are separate decisions. Drafting context.

sources.title: Salem Web Network–Gloo asset purchase agreement (2023), fulfillment liability
sources.proposition: The Salem agreement's assumed liabilities included fulfilling job listings and subscriptions sold before closing, all set forth on a schedule, including refunds to subscribers who cancel.
sources.verbatimQuote: The Assumed Liabilities include the liability to fulfill contracts for all job listings and subscriptions to products and services on the Websites sold by Seller prior to the Closing Date, all of which liabilities are set forth on Schedule 1.3(a) (such liabilities, the “Fulfillment Liability”), including the liability to pay refunds to any subscribers who cancel (for whatever reason) their subscriptions to any of the Website’s products and services sold by Seller.

sources.title: Internet-services asset purchase agreement (2007)
sources.proposition: The Internet-services agreement supports an express buyer obligation to serve customers whose deferred revenue the seller already received.
sources.verbatimQuote: The Buyer shall assume and discharge the obligation to provide Internet Services to the Customers who have paid the Deferred Revenue to Seller.

sources.title: Barlow & Williams: Purchase price adjustments, prepaid subscriptions
sources.proposition: Barlow & Williams advise that sellers with many prepaid annual subscriptions should be prepared for the buyer to ask for a price reduction for the ongoing liabilities it assumes.
sources.verbatimQuote: If there are lots of prepaid annual subscriptions, sellers should be prepared for the buyer to ask for a reduction in purchase price to account for the ongoing operating liabilities the buyer is assuming.

requirements.requirementGuidance: Only if refund exposure exists, review the following safeguard. Otherwise mark it not applicable. Test a post-closing refund of a pre-closing sale against the allocation rule. The agreement SHOULD allocate responsibility for customer refunds associated with periods spanning closing. Causation and time rules are defined, and the same exposure is not counted twice in price and indemnity. Drafting context.

sources.title: Grove–VitaMedica asset purchase agreement (2021), customer refunds
sources.proposition: The Grove agreement required the selling parties to reimburse the buyer for customer refund claims on products sold before closing, with the buyer responsible for the first $10,000 in the aggregate.
sources.verbatimQuote: With respect to sales of Products made prior to Closing, Selling Parties will promptly reimburse Buyer in immediately available funds within ten (10) days of delivery of written notice from Buyer for any claims for refunds by Customers that are authorized by Seller or are in accordance with the agreements with the applicable Customer (even if not authorized by Seller); provided, however, that Buyer shall be responsible for the first $10,000 in the aggregate of those refunds (i.e., Buyer shall not charge Selling Parties for those until the sum of payments and costs exceeds $10,000).

sources.title: Salem Web Network–Gloo asset purchase agreement (2023), fulfillment liability
sources.proposition: The Salem agreement's assumed liabilities included fulfilling job listings and subscriptions sold before closing, all set forth on a schedule, including refunds to subscribers who cancel.
sources.verbatimQuote: The Assumed Liabilities include the liability to fulfill contracts for all job listings and subscriptions to products and services on the Websites sold by Seller prior to the Closing Date, all of which liabilities are set forth on Schedule 1.3(a) (such liabilities, the “Fulfillment Liability”), including the liability to pay refunds to any subscribers who cancel (for whatever reason) their subscriptions to any of the Website’s products and services sold by Seller.

requirements.requirementGuidance: Only if chargeback exposure exists, review the following safeguard. Otherwise mark it not applicable. Test a delayed chargeback and processor reserve release against the rule. The agreement SHOULD allocate responsibility for chargebacks and related processor deductions. Settlement timing, evidence and reimbursement mechanics are negotiated. Drafting context.

sources.title: Odimo–Ashford.com asset purchase agreement (2002), chargebacks retained by seller
sources.proposition: The Odimo agreement left with the seller every liability the buyer did not expressly assume, including liabilities arising from credit card fraud or chargebacks.
sources.verbatimQuote: Buyer shall not assume or be obligated to pay, perform or otherwise discharge any liability or obligation of Seller, direct or indirect, known or unknown, absolute or contingent, not expressly and specifically assumed by Buyer as an Assumed Liability, including, without limitation, any liabilities related to or arising from credit card fraud or chargebacks (all such liabilities and obligations not being assumed being herein called the "EXCLUDED LIABILITIES").

sources.title: Aterian–Squatty Potty asset purchase agreement (2021), returns and chargebacks after closing
sources.proposition: The Aterian agreement made the seller responsible for returns and chargebacks, during the first year after closing, of products it sold before closing, to the extent they exceed $30,000 in the aggregate.
sources.verbatimQuote: Seller agrees that if any retailer to whom Seller or any of its Affiliates sold or otherwise transferred product(s) prior to the Closing (and such product(s) would otherwise constitute an Acquired Asset) returns or chargebacks any of such product(s) during the period from and after the Closing and until the date that is the first anniversary of the Closing Date, then Seller shall be responsible for the amount of any such product(s) so returned or charged back that is, in the aggregate, in excess of Thirty Thousand Dollars ($30,000) (the “Excess Returns and Chargebacks”).

requirements.requirementGuidance: Only if subscriptions are included, review the following safeguard. Otherwise mark it not applicable. Locate billing, service and customer-notification responsibilities during migration. The agreement SHOULD specify how customer subscriptions continue or migrate at closing. Payment credentials and recurring mandates require provider-specific review. Drafting context.

sources.title: Barlow & Williams: Purchase price adjustments, prepaid subscriptions
sources.proposition: Barlow & Williams describe customers on pre-existing annual subscriptions as customers the buyer must serve who generate no revenue until renewal.
sources.verbatimQuote: From the buyer’s perspective, people on pre-existing annual subscriptions are customers who need to be served but who will generate no revenue until their subscription renews.

sources.verbatimQuote: The Assumed Liabilities include the liability to fulfill contracts for all job listings and subscriptions to products and services on the Websites sold by Seller prior to the Closing Date, all of which liabilities are set forth on Schedule 1.3(a) (such liabilities, the “Fulfillment Liability”), including the liability to pay refunds to any subscribers who cancel (for whatever reason) their subscriptions to any of the Website’s products and services sold by Seller.

requirements.requirementGuidance: Locate an agreed acceptance procedure for the relevant site, services and administrative control. The agreement SHOULD provide objective checks that the purchaser can operate the transferred business at handover. Material failures and acceptance timing are defined without requiring every possible online system. Drafting context.

sources.title: Smart Repair Pro–Beard Revive purchase agreement (2021), inspection period
sources.proposition: The Jeffs Brands agreement gave the buyer fourteen days after migration to inspect the assets while operating them as close as possible to the seller's operation.
sources.verbatimQuote: Buyer shall have a period of fourteen (14) days from the Completed Migration to fully inspect the Assets (“Inspection Period”) upon the following terms and conditions: (a) During the Inspection Period, Buyer shall operate the Assets in a manner as close as possible to Seller’s operation and shall not make any material changes, including addition of new expenses, without Seller’s prior written consent.

sources.title: Bankrate asset purchase agreement (2016), transition assistance
sources.proposition: The Bankrate agreement required the owner and seller after closing to use best efforts to document and explain the acquired trade secrets, know-how and other intellectual property so the buyer could use it without relying on the owner's special knowledge or memory.
sources.verbatimQuote: Without limiting the generality of Section 7.7(b), after the Closing, each of Owner and Seller agrees that he or it shall use best efforts to promptly take all such actions as may be requested by Buyer from time to time to cause all trade secrets, know-how and other Intellectual Property included in the Purchased Assets to (i) be sufficiently documented to allow its full and proper use without reliance on the special knowledge or memory of Owner or any other Person and (ii) be sufficiently explained and demonstrated to such Persons as the Buyer may direct to allow its full and proper use without reliance on the special knowledge or memory of Owner or any other Person.
sources.pullQuoteLocator: Without limiting the generality of Section|Owner or any other Person.

requirements.requirementGuidance: Test recovery contacts, multifactor authentication, secrets rotation and retained support access against the handover plan. The agreement SHOULD specify how administrative access is transferred and seller access is removed or limited. Only authorized business access is shared; personal identities are not transferred and provider controls are not bypassed. Drafting context.

sources.title: Innovative Gourmet–iGourmet asset purchase agreement (2024), administrative access
sources.proposition: The iGourmet agreement required the seller to give the buyer administrative-level access to the software and application items listed in its disclosure schedules.
sources.verbatimQuote: Promptly following the execution of this Agreement, Seller shall provide Buyer with administrative level access to the software/application items listed on Section 5.01 of the Disclosure Schedules.

sources.proposition: The Mount Snow agreement required the seller and its affiliates to stop using the business domain names, and similar domain names, after a stated date.

Snow”, “Mount Snow”, “Attitash”, or “Bear Peak” at the close of the 2006/2007 ski season and all times thereafter.

sources.title: Removing an outside collaborator from an organization repository (GitHub Docs)
sources.proposition: GitHub states that the repository owner is responsible for ensuring that people who lose access delete confidential information and that a removed collaborator keeps any local clones.
sources.verbatimQuote: You are responsible for ensuring that people who have lost access to a repository delete any confidential information or intellectual property. While forks of private repositories are deleted when a collaborator is removed, the person will still retain any local clones of your repository.

sources.title: Removing a member account, IAM access roles (AWS Organizations User Guide)
sources.proposition: AWS states that an IAM role created for access by the management account is not automatically deleted when a member account is removed.
sources.verbatimQuote: When you remove a member account from the organization, any IAM role that was created to enable access by the organization's management account isn't automatically deleted.
